### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary With `OffloadingConnector` + `CPUOffloadingSpec`, KV blocks are written to host memory correctly but are **never read back** while speculative decoding is enabled. Disabling `--speculative-config` — changing nothing else — makes the same workload serve from the CPU tier immediately. The CPU tier appears not to *retain* entries: `kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` rises while a request is in flight and returns to `0.0` as soon as the engine goes idle, never accumulating across requests. Lookups run ( `kv_offload_lookup_sync_delay_seconds_count` increments) and always miss, and the `CPU_to_GPU` transfer metric is absent entirely rather than merely small. ## Environment - Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, single card, `device_config=xpu`, TP=1 - vLLM built from source, `main` @ `3756bf1e2ba0909500fbe77e03fe02eafb7f7080` - vllm-xpu-kernels @ `4509e9f9791299e24622cb1d4ff63b61cd03925a` - Model: `Vishva007/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound-GPTQ` — `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, dense, 64 layers with hybrid linear_attn / full_attention, 24 Q / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1` - `--dtype float16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --max-model-len 179200 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --enable-chunked-prefill` - `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"CPUOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":17179869184}}'` Startup logs this, as expected: ``` Creating offloading spec with name: CPUOffloadingSpec KV offloading: EAGLE/MTP draft attention groups [0, 1, 2, 3] detected. The trailing chunk of these groups will be excluded from offloading due to volatility. ``` Note the fallback at `offloading/scheduler.py:218-219` marks **every** group as an eagle group, because no group self-identifies via `is_eagle_group` on this model (MTP shares the target's weights/KV). ## Reproduction `max_tokens=1` on every request, so wall time is essentially prefill. 1. send prompt A (~29.8K tokens) — cold 2. send A again — GPU prefix-cache hit 3. send 7 distinct ~35K-token prompts — flushes the 179,200-token GPU cache 4. send A again — GPU-evicted; should be served from the CPU tier Host pool is sized so the flush cannot evict A from CPU: 8 prompts × ~1.4 GB ≈ 11.5 GB against a 16 GiB pool, and the run's own `kv_offload_total_bytes_total{GPU_to_CPU}` confirms 11.69 GB stored. ## Results | step | `--speculative-config` MTP **on** | MTP **off** | |---|---|---| | 1. cold | 17.84 s | 16.59 s | | 2. GPU-cached | 1.92 s | 0.74 s | | 4. post-evict | **16.78 s** (recomputed) | **1.61 s** (served) | MTP off, the arithmetic closes exactly: ``` step 4 (CPU fetch) 1.61 s step 2 (GPU cache) 0.74 s ------- difference 0.87 s ≈ kv_offload_load_time_total = 0.851 s ``` ### Metrics, MTP on ``` kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"} = 1.1685986304e+10 (11.69 GB, 24 transfers) kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="CPU_to_GPU"} = (absent) kv_offload_store_bytes_total = 1.1685986304e+10 kv_offload_lookup_sync_delay_seconds_count = 10 ``` Per-window `kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` against `Running`: ``` Running: 0 usage 0.0 Running: 1 usage 0.0844 <- 8.44% of 16 GiB = ~1.45 GB = exactly one prompt Running: 0 usage 0.0 Running: 1 usage 0.0844 Running: 0 usage 0.0 ``` It never exceeded 0.088 across the whole run, so LRU eviction was never in play. ### Metrics, MTP off (only change) ``` kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="CPU_to_GPU"} = 1.097662464e+09 (1.10 GB) kv_offload_load_bytes_total = 1.097662464e+09 kv_offload_load_time_total = 0.851 s kv_offload_load_size_count = 1 ``` `kv_cache_size_tokens` also rises 179,200 → 215,647 with the draft model gone, but that only changes how much is evicted, not whether reads happen at all. ## What I ruled out - **Undersized pool.** Usage peaks at one prompt and returns to zero; the pool never fills. Raising 8 GiB → 16 GiB changed nothing. - **A lookup-side off-by-one.** `is_eagle_unverified` widens the query by one chunk only for sliding-window groups (`scheduler.py:695-700`) but applies `num_hit_chunks -= 1` unconditionally (`:733`). This model has no sliding window (`sliding_window="None"`), so the decrement is uncompensated. I patched `:696` to widen for all eagle groups and it made **no difference** — and on reflection an ~18-chunk prompt losing one chunk should produce a partial hit, not a total miss. So this asymmetry looks wrong but is not the cause. - **`offload_prompt_only`.** Already defaults to `True` (`v1/kv_offload/base.py:597`), so the volatile decode tail should already be excluded. The evidence points at the **store/retention** path rather than lookup: entries are written and counted, then not committed for future lookup, so lookups search an empty index. Other `is_eagle_group` sites I have not traced are `scheduler.py:359` (store-side chunk decrement while decoding) and the `is_store_reachable_swa_chunk` gate. ## Ask Is `OffloadingConnector` expected to work with EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding at all, particularly on hybrid Mamba/GDN + attention models? If the volatility handling is meant to exclude only the trailing chunk, something is dropping the whole entry instead. Happy to run instrumented builds — the reproduction is deterministic and takes about three minutes. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
